From 477f3488a94e35380c82a7498d46f10fa5f3edd2 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Christophe Leroy <christophe.leroy@c-s.fr>
Date: Fri, 14 Feb 2020 06:53:00 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] powerpc/6xx: Fix power_save_ppc32_restore() with
 CONFIG_VMAP_STACK

power_save_ppc32_restore() is called during exception entry, before
re-enabling the MMU. It substracts KERNELBASE from the address
of nap_save_msscr0 to access it.

With CONFIG_VMAP_STACK enabled, data MMU translation has already been
re-enabled, so power_save_ppc32_restore() has to access
nap_save_msscr0 by its virtual address.

Reported-by: Larry Finger <Larry.Finger@lwfinger.net>
Signed-off-by: Christophe Leroy <christophe.leroy@c-s.fr>
Fixes: cd08f109e262 ("powerpc/32s: Enable CONFIG_VMAP_STACK")
Tested-by: Larry Finger <Larry.Finger@lwfinger.net>
Signed-off-by: Michael Ellerman <mpe@ellerman.id.au>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/7bce32ccbab3ba3e3e0f27da6961bf6313df97ed.1581663140.git.christophe.leroy@c-s.fr

diff --git a/arch/powerpc/kernel/idle_6xx.S b/arch/powerpc/kernel/idle_6xx.S
index 0ffdd18b9f26..433d97bea1f3 100644
--- a/arch/powerpc/kernel/idle_6xx.S
+++ b/arch/powerpc/kernel/idle_6xx.S
@@ -166,7 +166,11 @@ BEGIN_FTR_SECTION
 	mfspr	r9,SPRN_HID0
 	andis.	r9,r9,HID0_NAP@h
 	beq	1f
+#ifdef CONFIG_VMAP_STACK
+	addis	r9, r11, nap_save_msscr0@ha
+#else
 	addis	r9,r11,(nap_save_msscr0-KERNELBASE)@ha
+#endif
 	lwz	r9,nap_save_msscr0@l(r9)
 	mtspr	SPRN_MSSCR0, r9
 	sync
@@ -174,7 +178,11 @@ BEGIN_FTR_SECTION
 1:
 END_FTR_SECTION_IFSET(CPU_FTR_NAP_DISABLE_L2_PR)
 BEGIN_FTR_SECTION
+#ifdef CONFIG_VMAP_STACK
+	addis	r9, r11, nap_save_hid1@ha
+#else
 	addis	r9,r11,(nap_save_hid1-KERNELBASE)@ha
+#endif
 	lwz	r9,nap_save_hid1@l(r9)
 	mtspr	SPRN_HID1, r9
 END_FTR_SECTION_IFSET(CPU_FTR_DUAL_PLL_750FX)
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/powerpc/kernel/idle_6xx.S`**
   - The patch modifies the assembly code in the `power_save_ppc32_restore()` function.
   - It introduces conditional compilation using `#ifdef CONFIG_VMAP_STACK` to handle the access to `nap_save_msscr0` and `nap_save_hid1`.
   - When `CONFIG_VMAP_STACK` is enabled, the code now accesses `nap_save_msscr0` and `nap_save_hid1` using their virtual addresses directly (using `addis r9, r11, nap_save_msscr0@ha` and `addis r9, r11, nap_save_hid1@ha`).
   - If `CONFIG_VMAP_STACK` is not enabled, it continues to subtract `KERNELBASE` from the addresses as before.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modifications are directly related to the handling of memory addresses in the context of the `CONFIG_VMAP_STACK` configuration. 
- The changes ensure that when the data MMU translation is re-enabled (as is the case with `CONFIG_VMAP_STACK`), the function correctly accesses the required variables using their virtual addresses instead of physical addresses adjusted by `KERNELBASE`.
- This fix addresses a bug that could occur during exception entry when the MMU is not yet re-enabled, ensuring that the system behaves correctly under different configurations.

powerpc/6xx: Fix power_save_ppc32_restore() with
 CONFIG_VMAP_STACK

power_save_ppc32_restore() is called during exception entry, before
re-enabling the MMU. It substracts KERNELBASE from the address
of nap_save_msscr0 to access it.

With CONFIG_VMAP_STACK enabled, data MMU translation has already been
re-enabled, so power_save_ppc32_restore() has to access
nap_save_msscr0 by its virtual address.

Reported-by: Larry Finger <Larry.Finger@lwfinger.net>
Signed-off-by: Christophe Leroy <christophe.leroy@c-s.fr>
Fixes: cd08f109e262 ("powerpc/32s: Enable CONFIG_VMAP_STACK")
Tested-by: Larry Finger <Larry.Finger@lwfinger.net>
Signed-off-by: Michael Ellerman <mpe@ellerman.id.au>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/7bce32ccbab3ba3e3e0f27da6961bf6313df97ed.1581663140.git.christophe.leroy@c-s.fr

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs because the `power_save_ppc32_restore()` function attempts to access the `nap_save_msscr0` variable using a physical address calculation (subtracting `KERNELBASE`) when the data MMU translation has already been re-enabled with `CONFIG_VMAP_STACK`. This leads to incorrect memory access, as the function should use the virtual address directly in this scenario.

Here is the patch:
 	andis.	r9,r9,HID0_NAP@h
 	beq	1f
+#ifdef CONFIG_VMAP_STACK
+	addis	r9, r11, nap_save_msscr0@ha
+#else
 	addis	r9,r11,(nap_save_msscr0-KERNELBASE)@ha
+#endif
 	lwz	r9,nap_save_msscr0@l(r9)
 	mtspr	SPRN_MSSCR0, r9
 END_FTR_SECTION_IFSET(CPU_FTR_NAP_DISABLE_L2_PR)
 BEGIN_FTR_SECTION
+#ifdef CONFIG_VMAP_STACK
+	addis	r9, r11, nap_save_hid1@ha
+#else
 	addis	r9,r11,(nap_save_hid1-KERNELBASE)@ha
+#endif
 	lwz	r9,nap_save_hid1@l(r9)
 	mtspr	SPRN_HID1, r9

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```assembly
addis	r9,r11,(nap_save_msscr0-KERNELBASE)@ha
lwz	r9,nap_save_msscr0@l(r9)
```
Reason:
The `power_save_ppc32_restore()` function incorrectly calculates the address of `nap_save_msscr0` by subtracting `KERNELBASE`, which is appropriate only when the data MMU translation is disabled. With `CONFIG_VMAP_STACK` enabled, the data MMU translation is already re-enabled, making this calculation invalid and leading to incorrect memory access.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```assembly
#ifdef CONFIG_VMAP_STACK
	addis	r9, r11, nap_save_msscr0@ha
#else
	addis	r9,r11,(nap_save_msscr0-KERNELBASE)@ha
#endif
```
Reason:
The patch introduces a conditional compilation directive that checks if `CONFIG_VMAP_STACK` is enabled. If it is, the code accesses `nap_save_msscr0` using its virtual address directly, avoiding the incorrect physical address calculation. This ensures that the correct memory location is accessed, resolving the bug.
